fields.sample_size: close study of three state-NGO partnerships in Pakistan (privatisation of basic health units, an adopt-a-school programme, low-cost sanitation through the Orangi Pilot Project); fieldwork with officials, NGO representatives and donor advisers, with follow-up in 2016
fields.effect_estimate: The collaborations improved service delivery, but only the Orangi Pilot Project (low-cost sanitation) became an embedded partnership able to change government working practices; the other two did not, because public servants tolerated rather than welcomed NGOs under political or donor pressure and donor-funded NGO leaders lacked the ideational commitment embedded partnerships require. In the sanitation programme 145,466 households invested US$3.2 million in in-house latrines and external sewers with government investing in trunk infrastructure. Qualitative case analysis; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: qualitative comparative case study of three state-NGO partnerships
fields.section: Full text: Introduction; three case sections (health, education, sanitation); Conclusion with Table 1 (partnership types)
fields.exact_location: Introduction; three case sections (health, education, sanitation); Conclusion with Table 1 (partnership types)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a three-case study of state-NGO partnerships in Pakistan including low-cost sanitation (Orangi Pilot Project: 145,466 households invested US$3.2 million), read in full text 2026-10-04. Only the sanitation partnership became embedded; officials tolerated NGOs under political or donor pressure.
